newsitem.title: CANADA: Imperial Oil applies to expand Cold Lake.
newsitem.headline: Imperial Oil applies to expand Cold Lake.

text.p: Imperial Oil Ltd said on Friday it made an application to Alberta regulators for a previously announced C$520-million expansion of its huge Cold Lake heavy oil project in the province's northeast.

Imperial said that if it garnered approvals from the Alberta Energy and Utilities Board and Alberta Environmental Protection later this year and market conditions remained favorable, construction on the project could begin in late 1997.

The company is applying to begin developing a new operating site called Mahkeses, expected to produce an additional 30,000 barrels a day of bitumen, and a 220-megawatt electrical power co-generation facility at the Mahkeses plant.
Imperial also wants to undertake new development work to bolster bitumen and steam production from the company's existing Cold Lake operations.

The cost of the development -- which will add proven bitumen reserves of 290 million barrels -- would be about C$440 million, increasing to C$520 million by 2006 with the addition of further field facilities, Imperial said.
The company said it expected the Mahkeses plant to be operational in 1999.
